meta.subtitle: AI-driven growth is real, but a convertible-funded balance sheet, non-GAAP-based multiples and cycle risk leave the reward/risk short of a BUY

analystSentiment.commentary:
We rate Advanced Energy a HOLD with a $290–$410 target range over a 12-month horizon. The business is doing well on the company's own numbers: second-quarter 2026 revenue rose {+ 30% year over year +} and came in above the high end of guidance, according to the August 3, 2026 earnings release. Our hesitation is about price and about which earnings the price rests on.

The forward multiples that make the stock look reasonable are built on consensus EPS that we read as non-GAAP, while GAAP earnings carry the costs of the 2026 convertible refinancing. The stock also sits well below its 52-week high, and nothing in the 10-Q, the release or the 10-K explains that fall. This is a cyclical supplier whose revenue fell in two consecutive years as recently as FY23 and FY24, so a real Bear case carries real weight.

The scenario math (see Valuation) derives HOLD: expected upside clears the BUY bar, but reward/risk does not. We would rather wait for the third-quarter print and a settled share count than pay for the Street's path in advance.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. provides precision power conversion, measurement, and control solutions. Its plasma power products serve semiconductor and thin film plasma processes such as dry etch and deposition, and its high and low voltage power products go into semiconductor equipment, data center computing, industrial production, medical and life science equipment, networking, and telecommunications. It also sells sensing, controls and instrumentation products and a repair, calibration and refurbishment service business.

The company operates as a single segment of power electronics conversion products, sold into four markets: Semiconductor Equipment, Data Center Computing, Industrial and Medical, and Telecom and Networking. It sells to OEMs, distributors and end customers, and the 2025 Form 10-K says sales are primarily made on a purchase order basis without long-term purchase commitments. The company was incorporated in 1981 and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

FY25 revenue was $1.8B, up 21.4%. In our reading, Advanced Energy is a cyclical equipment supplier that currently has AI-related demand working in its favor in more than one market at once.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
Advanced Energy is executing well: revenue growth has accelerated, gross margin has stepped up, and management guides the third quarter of 2026 higher again. The convertible refinancing completed in May 2026 left the company with more cash than debt.

The price already reflects much of this. At $297.29 the stock trades on a high trailing GAAP multiple, and the forward multiples rest on consensus EPS that we read as non-GAAP. The new and old convertible notes add dilution that GAAP results and the share count have not fully absorbed. The revenue history also shows how quickly this business can turn down.

We weight a Base case built on FY27E consensus EPS most heavily, but a credible Bear case keeps reward/risk below the BUY threshold. HOLD.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, measured against the revenue and EPS guidance in the August 3, 2026 release (see Valuation).
Data Center Computing: the 10-Q expects AI-driven demand and adoption of next generation high power solutions to support growth in the remainder of 2026 (see Growth).
Semiconductor Equipment: the company expects demand for leading-edge logic and memory to keep supporting its products in the remainder of the year.
Settlement of the 2028 Notes redemption set for September 23, 2026, which will show the post-refinancing share count (see Financials).
risks: Cyclicality: revenue fell in both FY23 and FY24 before recovering (see Financials).
Dilution from the convertible notes, which also widens the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP earnings (see Risks).
A sharp, unexplained fall from the 52-week high (see Valuation).
Component lead times and prices are rising with AI-related demand, which the 10-Q says could become material (see Risks).

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The annual record shows a cyclical business. Revenue fell {- 10.3% -} in FY23 and {- 10.5% -} in FY24, and operating margin dropped to 2.5% in FY24 before recovering to 9.3% in FY25 on revenue growth of {+ 21.4% +}. Gross margin held in a narrow band, from 35.7% to 37.7%, across FY21–FY25.

The second quarter of 2026 moved well above that band. Revenue was $574.1M against $441.5M a year earlier, gross margin was 41.1% against 37.0%, and operating income was $95.1M against $31.6M. The company attributes the growth to AI-related demand for leading-edge logic and memory in Semiconductor Equipment, higher AI investment by hyperscale customers in Data Center Computing, and a continued recovery in Industrial and Medical.

GAAP and non-GAAP earnings diverge sharply. GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations was $1.29, against $0.67 a year earlier, and included $31.8 million, or $0.75 per diluted share, of inducement costs on the partial conversion of the 2028 notes. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.74. Diluted weighted-average shares rose to 42.3 from 37.8 a year earlier.

The margin step-up looks real to us, but GAAP earnings will keep carrying convertible-related costs and a larger diluted share count.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
At December 31, 2025, total debt of $567.5M sat entirely in current debt, which is why the FY25 current ratio was only 1.59. Net debt was negative, a net cash position of $223.7M.

On May 18, 2026, the company issued $1.15 billion of 0% Convertible Notes due 2031 and received net proceeds of approximately $1,128.1 million. At the same time it exchanged approximately $438.3 million principal of its 2.5% 2028 Notes for approximately $442.4 million in cash and approximately 2.0 million shares. The 10-Q says the remaining net proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes and debt repayment.

At June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $1,396.5 million, current debt was $135.6 million and long-term debt was $1,128.6 million, so cash still exceeded total debt. The TTM current ratio is 3.79. Inventories rose to $538.1 million from $411.2 million at year-end, which fits the higher revenue run rate but adds exposure if demand turns.

The remaining $136.7 million of 2028 Notes was called for redemption on September 23, 2026, with a conversion price of approximately $137.46. The company settles principal in cash and the remainder in shares. The 10-Q predates that date, so the outcome is not in hand. Liquidity is strong; the cost of this structure is dilution rather than interest.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation has trailed earnings growth because of capacity spending. FY25 free cash flow was $125.9M, a 7.0% FCF margin, after capital expenditure of $107.4M. The 2025 proxy reports operating cash flow from continuing operations of $235 million for that year. FCF margin has ranged between 5.0% and 8.9% over FY21–FY25, which is modest for a stock valued at these multiples.

The second quarter of 2026 was stronger: the release reports $86 million of cash flow from continuing operations and $4.1 million of quarterly dividends. The 10-K says the company accelerated investments in capacity to meet Data Center Computing demand, so we do not expect capital spending to fall soon.

Shareholder returns are small. FY25 share repurchases were $30.2M and dividends paid were $15.6M, and the dividend yield is 0.13%. The TTM FCF yield of 0.7% means the shares are priced on future growth, not current cash.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing figures the stock is expensive: P/E (TTM) is 55.3x, EV/EBITDA (TTM) is 35.5x and P/S is 5.8x. The trailing P/E is based on GAAP earnings, which include the inducement costs described in Financials.

The forward multiples look much lower, with two caveats. First, the vendor's "NTM" P/E of 26.4x matches the price over FY26E EPS of $11.24, so it is in effect a current-year multiple. On FY27E EPS of $15.34 the multiple is ~19.4x. Second, consensus EPS is very likely non-GAAP: FY26E sits far above FY25 GAAP diluted EPS of $3.84 and in line with the company's non-GAAP run rate. These forward multiples should not be read as GAAP multiples.

The Street is bullish. Eleven of 12 analysts rate the stock a Buy and one a Hold, with a consensus target of $429.08, a median of $412.50 and a range of $370.00–$535.00. The vendor's peer list is made up of companies that are not power-conversion or semiconductor-equipment businesses, so we make no peer-multiple comparison.

The price matters as much as the multiple. At $297.29 the stock sits well below its 52-week high of $397.44 and well above its low of $169.36. None of the sources explains the fall from the high, so we read it as a warning that the market is questioning either the durability of AI-related demand or the multiple, not as a free discount.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Data Center Computing and Semiconductor Equipment demand both hold through 2027, FY27E consensus EPS is delivered, and the market pays close to the Street's consensus target of $429.08.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: FY27E EPS of $15.34 comes through on a non-GAAP basis, and the market values it at a multiple between today's ~19.4x on FY27E and the 26.4x it pays on FY26E. This sits below the Street low target of $370.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI-related and semiconductor equipment orders pause, as revenue did in FY23–FY24. Earnings stall near FY26E EPS of $11.24, and the market pays only the lower FY27E-based multiple named in Base.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Our horizon is 12 months. The Base case carries the most weight because the second-quarter results and third-quarter guidance support the consensus growth path. We still value FY27E earnings below the multiple the market now pays on FY26E, because those earnings are non-GAAP, the share count is rising, and the market will need to look past 2027 to hold today's current-year multiple.

The Bull case takes the Street at its word. We give it a 25% weight, below the Base, because the consensus target assumes the stock regains and passes its 52-week high without any evidence on hand of why it fell from there.

The Bear case gets a 30% weight. The FY23–FY24 record shows this revenue base can fall two years running. The 10-K says sales are made on purchase orders that customers can delay or cancel. The sharp fall from the 52-week high shows the market is already willing to cut the multiple. In the Bear case both earnings and the multiple compress, which is the structure of the last downturn.

The weighted result clears the BUY threshold on expected upside but falls short on reward/risk, so the derived label is HOLD. The deciding split is Bear against Base. Moving weight from Bear to Base would push the call toward BUY, and the strength of the second quarter argues for that. We keep the Bear weight because the cause of the recent fall is unknown and the order book carries no long-term commitments. The call is close on expected upside and less close on reward/risk.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Advanced Energy reports a single segment of power electronics conversion products, so no segment split is reported below the consolidated total. Within it, the company sells into Semiconductor Equipment, Data Center Computing, Industrial and Medical, and Telecom and Networking. Its products range from plasma power for etch and deposition to high and low voltage power for server racks, medical devices and networking equipment, plus a service business covering repair, calibration, upgrades and refurbishment. The breadth of end markets is the main structural feature: it spreads cycle risk, but each market has its own competitors and design cycles, so the single segment does not mean a single competitive position.

moatFactors.name: Design-win incumbency
moatFactors.body: The 10-K says new products designed for capital equipment manufacturers typically have a lifespan of many years, and the company works with customers early in their design cycles. A win can therefore earn revenue for years. The same filing says design windows may be narrow, that there is no assurance of new wins, and that the company may not maintain single source status. Incumbency helps, but it is re-contested with every equipment generation.

moatFactors.name: End-market diversification
moatFactors.body: Selling into four markets lets growth in one offset weakness in another, as in 2025, when the proxy reports Data Center Computing growth while Industrial and Medical declined. The protection is partial: revenue still fell in both FY23 and FY24, so diversification softens the cycle without removing it.

moatFactors.name: Manufacturing footprint
moatFactors.body: The 2026 proxy says the company exited its last factory in China during 2025 and added capacity in the Philippines and Mexico, which helped it manage tariffs. That is an operating advantage while trade policy is in flux. The 10-Q lists the scaling of capacity and timely customer qualification of new manufacturing lines as risks, so the footprint is still being built out.

businessMoat.durability:
We rate the moat NARROW. Gross margin stayed between 35.7% and 37.7% through a full cycle from FY21 to FY25, including two years of falling revenue, which suggests some pricing resilience. Customers choose the products on power conversion efficiency, power density, low noise and the ability to tailor solutions, according to the 10-Q, and those are engineering attributes that take time to match.

The moat is not wide. The 10-Q lists pricing pressure from customers and competitors and concentration of the customer base among its risks, and the 10-K says competitors may be more successful in implementing an AI strategy. Sales on purchase orders without long-term commitments also mean the advantage has to be re-earned with each design cycle. The current margin expansion may owe as much to strong demand as to durable advantage, and we would want to see it hold through a softer quarter before rating the moat higher.

points: Data Center Computing is the main growth driver on the figures available. The 2026 proxy reports that this market's revenue grew 107% in 2025 to $587 million, on demand from hyperscale customers for new AI data center power solutions. The 10-Q says revenue rose again in 2026's first half compared with a year earlier and expects the trend to continue in the remainder of the year. The counterweight is concentration: the 10-Q ties the growth to investment by leading hyperscale customers, who buy on purchase orders.

Semiconductor Equipment has returned to growth. The proxy reports 2025 Semiconductor revenue of $840 million, up 6%, and the August 2026 release says Semiconductor revenue grew 33% year over year in the second quarter. The 10-Q ties this to demand for leading-edge logic and memory used in AI applications. This market is the one with the clearest cyclical history.

Industrial and Medical is recovering from a weak 2025. The proxy says revenue in this market fell 11% in 2025 after bottoming in Q1 2025, and the 10-Q says demand has returned to normalized levels, with improvement expected in the remainder of 2026. This is the least AI-dependent source of growth and a useful offset if AI spending slows.

Telecom and Networking remained stable in 2026's first half, with growth driven mainly by AI-related applications, according to the 10-Q. We treat it as a steady contributor rather than a driver of the thesis.

Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$2.4B (+35%) and FY27E revenue of $3B. Those estimates require AI-related demand to keep compounding across two markets at once. The company's own guidance supports the near term, but the 10-K warns that the company may not have accurately assessed the magnitude or sustainability of AI-driven demand.

management.leadership:
The 2026 proxy statement, filed March 26, 2026, names Stephen Kelley as President and Chief Executive Officer and Paul Oldham as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The other named executive officers for 2025 were Eduardo Bernal Acebedo (Chief Operations Officer), Elizabeth Vonne (General Counsel & Corporate Secretary) and John Donaghey (Chief Commercial Officer). Grant H. Beard is Chairman of the Board, so the chair and chief executive roles are held by different people.

The execution record in the sources is good. The second quarter of 2026 came in above the high end of guidance on both revenue and EPS, according to the release, and the 2025 manufacturing moves out of China were completed while tariffs were changing. The test ahead is whether the team can scale capacity for Data Center Computing without the forecasting and inventory problems the 10-K flags as risks.
management.capitalAllocation:
The main capital decision of 2026 was the convertible refinancing described in Financials. It replaced 2.5% coupon notes with 0% notes and left the company with more cash than debt, at the cost of more potential shares. The 10-Q lists dilution and counterparty default risk related to the convertible debt, hedge, warrant and capped call transactions among its risks, but the excerpt does not give the terms of those hedges, so we cannot judge how much dilution they offset.

Capital spending is going into capacity for AI-related demand, which we think is the right priority given the growth in Data Center Computing. Repurchases and dividends are small relative to the market value (see Financials). Management says the remaining offering proceeds are for general corporate purposes and debt repayment, which leaves open whether the large cash balance will fund acquisitions; the 10-Q lists acquisition integration among its risks. We view the allocation as reasonable but dilutive, and we want to see how much of the cash is put to work.
management.governance:
Governance information comes from the proxy statement dated March 26, 2026, and the excerpt is truncated, so it does not cover board independence or committee composition. The Chairman and the CEO are different people.

The proxy says a majority of the named executive officers' 2025 target pay was performance-based, tied to financial and stock price performance under the 2025 short-term and long-term incentive plans. The earnings release adds that management's incentive plans include certain non-GAAP measures as criteria. That matters here: executives are paid partly on the non-GAAP figures that exclude items such as the convertible inducement costs, so outside holders should track GAAP results and diluted share count alongside the company's preferred measures.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of March 1, 2026, the proxy reports that all executive officers and directors as a group (14 persons) beneficially owned 476,577 shares, or 1.3% of the 37,848,305 shares then outstanding. The holders above five percent were BlackRock, Inc. at 14.6%, The Vanguard Group at 13.0% and FMR LLC at 5.2%, each based on Schedule 13G/A filings with older as-of dates: June 30, 2025 for BlackRock, December 31, 2024 for Vanguard and December 31, 2025 for FMR. No holder is near a majority, so no single shareholder controls the company.

Insider alignment therefore comes mainly through performance-based pay rather than ownership. The March 2026 share count also predates the shares issued in the May 2026 note exchange, and our current share figure is derived from market value and price rather than a reported count, so we do not read precision into it.

idiosyncratic: Convertible dilution. The 2028 Notes convert at approximately $137.46, well below the current price, and the company settles the amount above principal in shares. The 2031 Notes add further potential shares, and the 10-Q lists dilution and counterparty default risk on the related hedge, warrant and capped call transactions. The mechanism is a rising diluted share count that caps per-share growth. Watch the diluted share count in the third-quarter 10-Q after the September 2026 redemption.

Customer concentration and order visibility. The 10-K says sales are primarily on purchase orders, customers may delay or cancel orders without penalties, and the company generally has no long-term purchase commitments; the 10-Q lists concentration of the customer base as a risk. A pause by a few hyperscale or equipment customers could cut revenue quickly. Watch Data Center Computing commentary and inventory levels.

Supply and cost pressure. The 10-Q says AI-related demand is extending lead times and increasing prices of certain components, and that these factors, while not material this quarter, could become material. The 10-K adds that some supplier contracts require fixed quarterly purchases. The mechanism is margin squeeze or excess inventory. Watch gross margin against the second-quarter level of 41.1%.

Design-win and technology risk. The 10-K says competitors may develop more successful products with the aid of AI technology and that design windows may be narrow. Losing a platform at a large customer would hurt revenue for years. Watch for new product adoption in Data Center Computing, which the 10-Q expects to support growth.
risks.systemic:
Advanced Energy sells into markets the 10-K calls highly cyclical, where downturns bring lower demand, overcapacity, high inventory and price erosion. The FY23–FY24 revenue declines show how this works in practice. Today the main systemic exposure is AI-related capital spending: both Semiconductor Equipment and Data Center Computing growth depend on it, so a broad slowdown in AI investment would hit two markets at once.

The 10-Q also cites tariffs and trade policy, geopolitical instability including the conflicts in the Middle East, volatility in energy markets and disruptions to global shipping. It says these were not material to results in the current quarter but could become material through higher energy and supply chain costs. Rates and inflation matter mainly through customers' access to capital and through the multiple the market will pay for growth. We see the AI capital-spending cycle as the risk that matters most.

body: HOLD, with a target range of $290–$410 over 12 months. Advanced Energy is growing quickly and its balance sheet is liquid, but the valuation already leans on non-GAAP consensus earnings for 2027, dilution from the convertible notes is still being absorbed, and the stock's fall from its 52-week high is unexplained. Our scenarios give expected upside that clears the BUY bar but reward/risk that does not.

We would upgrade to BUY if third-quarter 2026 results land above the top of the guided revenue and non-GAAP EPS ranges and the post-redemption diluted share count shows dilution is contained, which would justify moving weight from Bear to Base. We would downgrade if third-quarter revenue falls below the bottom of the guided range or gross margin falls back toward the FY21–FY25 band, which would signal that the cycle is turning.
